- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; apply a 3–5 day lag correction: if price spikes, forecast should dip slightly in next 2–3 periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overshoots early in the forecast window; cap forecast at 10–15% below 30-day true mean for first 5–7 periods.
- Sentiment volatility >0.25 in last 5 days correlates with forecast error; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to sentiment before weighting forecast adjustments.
